SMTO-PRX-0015 — Proxmox didn't accept the saved username or password

GUID: 5ac06e59-6014-4f1d-bc8d-b0673924cb0a
Slug: proxmox-authentication-failed
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • Proxmox refused to sign SMTO in because the saved username or password is missing, wrong, or no longer works. Proxmox didn't carry out your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. Make sure "username" includes its realm (for example root@pam), correct "password", and select Save. Proxmox needs the user name, its sign-in realm and the current password.
  2. Sign in to the Proxmox web interface with the same username and password to confirm they work. If they fail there too, the account or password has to be fixed on Proxmox itself.
  3. Send your request again as a new message, mentioning the Proxmox parameter with @. A new message picks up the corrected sign-in details.

What success looks like

  • The Agent connects to Proxmox and returns the VM list or status you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Proxmox server. Never type your password into the chat, a command or a screenshot; keep it only in the Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Proxmox authentication failed: the Gateway reported missing or rejected credentials or an authentication failure, or Proxmox returned 401.

What this means

  • The HTTP auth layer reports missing/rejected credentials or auth failure, or the response status is 401. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The HTTP auth layer reports missing/rejected credentials or auth failure, or the response status is 401.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing credentials, rejected login and provider status while keeping the exact profile/account scope.

How to fix it

  • Check the Proxmox Server parameter's username (user@realm, for example root@pam) and password against the /api2/json/access/ticket login, and confirm in PVE that the account and realm exist and are not disabled or expired. Update the record in Parameter Store; never pass credentials in task text, command arguments or diagnostic reports.
  • Correct the exact profile credentials or renew the intended session through the supported flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported private authentication flow succeeds for the intended account.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
